finding: R49 download DNS ownership (also relevant to F09 resource cleanup)
classification: Demonstrated follow-up to the inspected audit defect
root_cause: Default reqwest DNS schedules blocking NSS work. Dropping a cancelled request and shutting the runtime down with a timeout returns while that work remains alive.
correction: An async-polled reqwest resolver owns a getent process group with a three-second DNS deadline, 64 KiB output bound and at most sixteen usable addresses. It yields to the existing download cancellation loop; request/runtime teardown kills and reaps the owned group. No abandoned blocking task or extra worker pool. Existing transfer budgets are unchanged.
regression: Before-fix test fails after cancellation with stalled NSS still alive. Passing regression repeats twelve Cancel/Delete/Reset cycles, six resolving after redirects; asserts sub-500ms cancellation, disappeared resolver processes, exact thread-budget recovery, removed staging, preserved old installation on Cancel/Reset, and target removal on Delete. Natural DNS deadline expiry also reaps the resolver and creates no partial download.
